retailer-partnership.q: Why should a traditional retailer join Source Pro B2B2C?
a: p

Because the retail market has changed. Customers increasingly compare prices, look for convenience, and expect online ordering. Source Pro B2B2C helps traditional retailers offer the same digital convenience while continuing to operate under their own shop name and customer relationships. It helps them protect existing customers, win back lost customers, and create new revenue opportunities.

retailer-partnership.q: How does Source Pro B2B2C transform a small shop into a digital hypermarket?
a: p

Once onboarded, a retailer can digitally display and sell a large product catalog through the Source Pro B2B2C application. The retailer can share access with their known customers, show products virtually, receive orders, and fulfill them through the distributor network. This allows even a small shop with limited shelf space to offer a much larger range of products online.

retailer-partnership.q: Does the retailer need to keep all listed products in stock?
a: p

No. That is one of the biggest advantages. The retailer can sell products virtually first and purchase them from the distributor only after receiving confirmed customer orders. This reduces dead stock, avoids unnecessary capital blockage, and helps the retailer offer more variety without expanding the shop physically.

retailer-partnership.q: Will the retailer lose ownership of customers?
a: p

No. The retailer retains the customer relationship. Customers are onboarded through the retailer, orders are received by the retailer, billing can be done in the retailer’s trade name, and the retailer continues to serve the customer directly. Source Pro B2B2C acts as the digital backbone, not as a replacement for the shopkeeper.

retailer-partnership.q: Can a retailer offer discounts to customers?
a: p

Yes. The platform is designed to enable customized pricing. Since retailers can access products through a structured supply chain and avoid unnecessary stock investment, they can pass suitable discounts to customers while protecting their margins.

retailer-partnership.q: How does Source Pro B2B2C help retailers compete with quick-commerce platforms?
a: p

Quick-commerce companies attract customers through speed, convenience, product variety, and aggressive pricing. Source Pro B2B2C helps retailers respond by giving them a digital catalog, customer ordering capability, distributor fulfillment support, and data-based stock planning. Over time, retailers can keep fast-moving products ready and deliver selected items quickly within their locality.

retailer-partnership.q: Can a retailer list their own products or existing inventory?
a: p

Yes. The retailer can also use the platform to promote and sell products already available in the shop, making the store more visible to its regular customers and improving the chance of repeat purchases.

retailer-partnership.q: How will customers come to know that the shop is online?
a: p

Retailers can inform existing customers, friends, relatives, neighbors, and regular buyers within their local area that their shop is now digitally enabled. Because most local shops already have trust and personal relationships in their neighborhood, this becomes a powerful advantage.

retailer-partnership.q: Will customers support their local shop if the same convenience is available?
a: p

Yes. Many customers prefer to support known local retailers when pricing, product availability, and convenience are comparable. Source Pro B2B2C gives retailers the digital tools needed to convert goodwill into actual orders.

retailer-partnership.q: Does the retailer need to invest in technology?
a: p

No major technology investment is required from the retailer. The platform provides the digital storefront, product display, ordering flow, and access mechanism. The retailer only needs to learn the simple operating process and actively promote the service among customers.

retailer-partnership.q: How does the retailer earn through Source Pro B2B2C?
a: p

The retailer earns by selling products to customers through the platform while retaining suitable margins. Since products can be sold digitally before being purchased physically, the retailer can generate sales without locking money in slow-moving inventory.

retailer-partnership.q: Can Source Pro B2B2C help a retailer identify fast-moving products?
a: p

Yes. Once the retailer starts receiving orders digitally, sales data can help identify products that move regularly. The retailer can then keep limited stock of those fast-moving items and improve delivery speed for repeat customers.

retailer-partnership.q: Will this create employment at the retailer level?
a: p

Yes. As digital orders increase, retailers may require support for order handling, packing, delivery, and customer service. This can create local employment and turn the shop into a more active neighborhood commerce point.

retailer-partnership.q: Is Source Pro B2B2C useful only for large retailers?
a: p

No. It is especially useful for small and medium retailers because they face the greatest difficulty in competing with large online platforms. A small grocery, stationery shop, fancy store, medical store, hardware shop, supermarket, or neighborhood store can benefit from the model.

retailer-partnership.q: Why is it risky for retailers to ignore digital transformation?
a: p

Retailers who remain only offline may gradually lose customers to online and quick-commerce options. Source Pro B2B2C gives them a practical way to upgrade without abandoning their existing business model. It is not about changing who they are; it is about giving them the tools to survive and grow.

distributor-partnership-india.q: Who can become a Source Pro B2B2C distributor?
a: p

Existing distributors, aspiring entrepreneurs, retailers looking to expand, sales and marketing professionals, and business-minded individuals can apply, subject to eligibility, territory availability, documentation, and approval by App Sphere B2B India Private Limited.

distributor-partnership-india.q: What is the role of a Source Pro B2B2C distributor?
a: p

The distributor introduces Source Pro B2B2C to retailers in the assigned area, onboards them, supports their usage of the app, receives retailer orders, and ensures timely delivery of products to the retail outlets. The distributor becomes the operational bridge between the central supply system and the local retailer network.

distributor-partnership-india.q: How is Source Pro B2B2C distribution different from conventional distribution?
a: p

Conventional distribution usually requires warehouse space, stock investment, manual order collection, market visits, credit risk, dead stock, expiry risk, damaged goods, undercutting, and continuous pressure to achieve primary billing. Source Pro B2B2C reduces many of these pressures by focusing on digitally captured, demand-led orders and a structured supply model.

distributor-partnership-india.q: Does the distributor need to hold stock?
a: p

No. The model is designed around a zero-stock or minimal-stock distribution approach. The distributor primarily handles onboarding, relationship management, order coordination, and delivery. Stock is supplied through the central or hub-based system as per the operating structure.

distributor-partnership-india.q: Will the distributor get a separate business identity?
a: p

Yes. The distributor operates under their own trade name and receives access to the relevant dashboard or Customer Management System. This helps them manage retailers, orders, and business activity professionally.

distributor-partnership-india.q: What investment is required to become a distributor?
a: p

As per the current proposed structure, distributor onboarding may involve a one-time registration or onboarding charge and a refundable security deposit. Final commercial terms, eligibility, territory rights, taxes, and documentation will be confirmed through the formal agreement issued by the company.

distributor-partnership-india.q: What documents are generally required from a distributor?
a: p

Typical documents may include signed agreement or MoU, GST certificate, FSSAI certificate if applicable, cancelled cheque, UPI QR code, company logo, email ID, phone number, and other KYC or statutory documents required by the company.
p

The model is territory-based. Orders from retailers onboarded by a particular distributor are intended to flow through that distributor as per company policy and system allocation. Final territory rights and conditions will be governed by the distributor agreement.

distributor-partnership-india.q: How many distributors are planned in each area?
a: p

The rollout plan is designed to cover all assembly constituencies of a district. 4-5 distributors per constituency and additional distributors in densely populated areas. This structure is intended to ensure strong local support for retailers and efficient delivery reach.

distributor-partnership-india.q: What kind of sales volume can a distributor expect?
a: p

The business plan projects strong daily sales potential once sufficient retailers are onboarded and actively transacting. Actual sales will depend on territory potential, retailer activation, product availability, customer adoption, operational discipline, and market conditions. All projections should be treated as indicative and subject to performance.
p

The projected distributor margin may vary by category, product, and commercial arrangement. The earlier business plan refers to distributor margins in a broad range and also highlights the possibility of conventional distribution-like margins without the same level of stock risk. Final margins will be defined in the company’s price lists and agreements.

distributor-partnership-india.q: Is credit allowed for distributors to purchase products?
a: p

The model is primarily designed as a cash-and-carry or demand-led purchase model. Since the distributor handles products that are already ordered by retailers, the dependency on credit-based stock dumping is reduced.

distributor-partnership-india.q: How quickly will products reach the distributor from the central warehouse or hub?
a: p

The operating plan aims to ensure timely delivery from the central warehouse and, later, from district or regional hubs. Exact delivery timelines will depend on location, order cut-off, product availability, logistics planning, and hub rollout progress.
p
Yes. The rollout plan includes the establishment of district hubs over time to store fast-moving products closer to the market, reduce logistics cost, and improve delivery efficiency for retailers.

distributor-partnership-india.q: How many vehicles or staff may a distributor need?
a: p

At least one delivery vehicle is generally advisable, and additional vehicles or staff may be required as order volumes increase. Staffing needs will depend on the number of active retailers, daily order load, geography, and delivery commitments.

distributor-partnership-india.q: Why is this opportunity important for existing distributors?
a: p

Many existing distributors are struggling with shrinking sales, rising receivables, high stock pressure, increasing competition, and the cost of manual market coverage. Source Pro B2B2C gives distributors a chance to become digital distributors and remain relevant in a market that is rapidly moving online.

manufacturer-partnership.q: Why should a manufacturer partner with Source Pro B2B2C?
a: p

Source Pro B2B2C gives manufacturers a digital route to reach thousands of retailers through an organized distributor network. It improves product visibility, reduces dependence on purely manual order collection, and helps brands participate in the digital transformation of traditional retail.

manufacturer-partnership.q: How does Source Pro B2B2C improve product visibility?
a: p

Once products are listed, they become visible to distributors, retailers, and, through retailers, end customers. Instead of relying only on sales executives visiting selected outlets, manufacturers can make their full product range discoverable digitally.
p

Yes. Manufacturers can list their complete SKU range, subject to onboarding, commercial terms, product data, images, pricing, stock availability, and applicable statutory requirements. This enables retailers to discover products that may not be physically available in their shop at that moment.

manufacturer-partnership.q: How does the model support market intelligence?
a: p

Digital order data can help manufacturers understand product demand, regional sales patterns, customer preferences, fast-moving SKUs, and retailer response. This can support production planning, inventory planning, marketing strategy, and new product decisions.

manufacturer-partnership.q: Can Source Pro B2B2C reduce the need for large field sales teams?
a: p

The platform can act as a 24×7 digital sales channel for listed products. While brand-building and market activation may still be required, digital visibility and app-based ordering can reduce the limitations of manual visit-based selling.

manufacturer-partnership.q: How does Source Pro B2B2C help prevent stock dumping?
a: p

Because the model is built around demand visibility and digital ordering, brands can move toward better planning instead of pushing inventory blindly into the channel. This can reduce dead stock, expiry risk, and market dissatisfaction.

manufacturer-partnership.q: Can local and regional brands participate?
a: p

Yes. Source Pro B2B2C is designed to support both established and local brands. Local brands can gain wider visibility through the platform and reach retailers beyond their existing limited distribution footprint.

manufacturer-partnership.q: What advantage does a manufacturer get over traditional distribution?
a: p

Traditional distribution often leaves many outlets uncovered due to manpower limits and inconsistent sales visits. Source Pro B2B2C can digitally connect brands with a much wider retailer base while retaining the role of distributors and retailers in the supply chain.

manufacturer-partnership.q: How does the model help manufacturers support traditional retailers?
a: p

By partnering with Source Pro B2B2C, manufacturers can help their existing retailer base become digitally active rather than watching them lose customers to large online platforms. This creates a responsible, future-ready channel strategy.

manufacturer-partnership.q: Can manufacturers control pricing and product information?
a: p

The platform is designed to display structured product information and pricing across levels. Commercial pricing, margins, and price-list allocation can be managed as per the agreed framework and platform capability.
p

Manufacturers are expected to provide accurate product details, images, pricing, stock support, statutory compliance documents, and supply commitment. They are also encouraged to invest in brand awareness while Source Pro B2B2C supports digital availability through the retailer-distributor network.
